references.text: God introduces himself to Moses as 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob', which emphasizes the continuity of God's relationship with his people.
God reaffirms his identity as 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob', establishing his eternal name and remembrance.
God reminds Moses of his relationship with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when he sends him to free the children of Israel.
Stephen quotes this passage in his speech to show that God is not God of the dead but of the living, confirming Jesus' words.
